I always suggest Ibanez, Epiphone, or Jackson to people. All depends on what they are looking for as each fills a niche. Ibanez and Jackson are very similar to me just different body styles. Ibanez is more all round (and for acoustic is much better than the other two) and Jackson is more metal to me. Epiphone has fallen off since Les Pauls are not as desired anymore and they have not made a great one since they moved production out of Korea. But the bodies of the SG models are still well made and just need pickups added in order to have great tone (easy mod if someone decides to keep following the path of playing).

Yeah, I get that question a lot and I concluded that Ibanez is a good choice for a starter guitar. They have so many models that they can probably find something in their budget and it is, without variation, playable.

I've never come across an Ibanez that wasn't playable - unless it was broken due to shipping or mistreatment. The electronics hold up very well. They take a ton of abuse and still keep on keeping on. I'm not really fond of their earlier years - those had some quality issues. But, anything after 1975 is okay. Note, I'd never recommend a guitar that old (at least from Ibanez) as a first guitar.

I'd be more comfortable recommending those as first collection guitars, but not as first guitars. As much as I love my older Martin D-28's, I'd not recommend one of those as a first guitar.
